codes.meaning: The control board isn't detecting the freezer evaporator fan spinning when it's supposed to be running, often because the blade has iced over or jammed.
Same kind of fan-feedback problem, but on the fresh-food side. Often shows up after a door's been left open long enough to ice over the fan.
The sensor that tracks the fridge's defrost cycle isn't reporting a valid reading.
A brief dip in incoming power was detected — commonly after a short outage. Usually clears itself and isn't a sign of hardware failure.
The compressor pulled an abnormal amount of current. Worth a professional look before it damages the compressor.
A communication fault inside the unit, typically triggered when power is interrupted mid-startup.
Not a fault — the fridge is acting as a temporary Wi-Fi access point so it can be set up.
Cooling has been switched off deliberately, usually demo or shop mode rather than a failure.

OF OF.what_it_means: Not a fault. Cooling has been switched off on purpose — this is the demo or shop mode retailers use so a fridge can be lit and running without cooling.
OF OF.why_it_happens: It is usually switched on accidentally by a button combination, or left on after delivery from a showroom unit.
OF OF.what_to_try: Turn cooling back on using the button combination in your manual — it varies by model, and the display returns to normal once it takes.
OF OF.when_to_call: Only if cooling will not re-enable, which points at the control rather than the mode.

codes.meaning: Water has been detected inside the Autofill compartment.
Components inside the fridge have lost communication with one another.

PC ER.what_it_means: Components inside the fridge have lost communication with one another, so the control cannot coordinate them.
PC ER.why_it_happens: A wiring or connector fault between boards, rather than a cooling problem in its own right.
PC ER.what_to_try: Cutting power for a minute clears a one-off communication glitch. A code that comes straight back is naming a real fault.
PC ER.when_to_call: If it returns after a power cycle, it needs a technician.

codes.meaning: The heater that keeps the ice pipe clear is reporting a fault.

33E.what_it_means: The heater that keeps the ice pipe clear is reporting a fault, so ice may stop being delivered.
33E.why_it_happens: A failure in that heater or its circuit, rather than anything to do with how the ice maker is used.
33E.what_to_try: Nothing here is an owner check — the pipe heater sits inside the dispenser assembly.
33E.when_to_call: When you see it, particularly if ice has stopped reaching the dispenser.

codes.meaning: The ice maker is not completing its cycle as it should.
The fan serving the ice compartment is not running correctly.
The compressor is locked and cannot start.

freezer.note: This is Samsung's combined refrigerator/freezer error-code page — Samsung doesn't publish a separate list for standalone chest/upright freezers. These codes specifically govern freezer-side components on integrated fridge/freezer units.

codes.meaning: The control board isn't detecting the freezer evaporator fan spinning when it's supposed to, often because the blade has iced over or jammed.
The temperature sensor inside the freezer's ice-maker area is sending a faulty or out-of-range reading, so ice production can't be regulated properly.
The sensor that tracks frost buildup and triggers defrost cycles isn't reporting correctly, which can let frost accumulate and restrict cold airflow.
The control board detected the compressor drawing an abnormal amount of current and shut cooling down as a protective measure.
The compressor received insufficient voltage to operate, typically from a brief brownout, which interrupts the cooling cycle.
The compressor was exposed to a voltage spike above its safe operating range, likely from a power surge, triggering a protective shutdown.
The ice-maker sensor is reporting a faulty or out-of-range reading.
The heater that keeps the ice pipe clear is reporting a fault.
The ice maker is not completing its cycle as it should.
The fan serving the ice compartment is not running correctly.
The compressor is locked and cannot start.
A communication fault inside the unit, typically after power was cut mid-startup.

cooktop.note: Direct fetch of this official URL was blocked by a site-wide Samsung maintenance page during research; content was independently corroborated across 3 separate search queries targeting this exact official page rather than a third-party source.

codes.meaning: The cooktop's burner temperature sensor is reporting a fault, so the control board can't reliably read burner temperature.
A burner's sensed temperature has climbed above the level the cooktop expects to see, prompting a protective stop.
A different burner-sensor circuit is reporting an out-of-range or failed reading, on another zone.
Another sensor-related fault on the cooktop's control circuitry, grouped with C0-C2 as sensor errors.
The touch panel thinks a button is being held down continuously for too long, usually because the surface is wet or something is resting on the controls.
On induction models, the cooktop can't detect a compatible pan on the element — wrong size, non-magnetic, or missing entirely.

washer.note: Samsung shows the same condition under several codes depending on model and display generation (4C, 4E and nF are one fault). Those variants are recorded together.

codes.meaning: Water is not entering the washer correctly — the machine asked to fill and did not get what it expected.

4C.what_it_means: The washer asked for water and did not get what it expected, so it has stopped rather than run a cycle dry. Samsung shows this as 4C on newer panels, 4E on older ones and nF on some models — one fault, three displays.
4C.why_it_happens: Almost always something before the machine rather than inside it: a supply tap not fully open, a kinked fill hose behind the unit, or the small mesh screens where the hoses meet the washer silted up with scale and grit.
4C.what_to_try: Check both taps are fully open, then pull the machine out far enough to see the fill hoses are not kinked. If that looks fine, turn the taps off, unscrew the hoses at the machine end and look at the inlet screens for debris.
4C.when_to_call: If the supply is good and the screens are clear, the inlet valve on the machine is next, and that is where it stops being an owner check.

4E.what_it_means: The same not-filling fault as 4C, shown as 4E on older Samsung panels.
4E.why_it_happens: A closed or partly closed tap, a kinked fill hose, or blocked inlet screens where the hoses connect.
4E.what_to_try: Work from the wall in: taps fully open, hoses unkinked, then the inlet screens at the machine end.
4E.when_to_call: If water reaches the machine freely and it still will not fill, the inlet valve needs testing.

nF.what_it_means: The washer is not filling — the same fault Samsung shows as 4C and 4E on other panels.
nF.why_it_happens: A tap that is not fully open, a kinked fill hose, or the inlet screens where the hoses meet the machine blocked with scale and grit.
nF.what_to_try: Check both taps, straighten the hoses, then turn the taps off and inspect the inlet screens at the machine end.
nF.when_to_call: If water reaches the machine freely and it still will not fill, the inlet valve is next.

codes.meaning: The load is unbalanced inside the tub, so the washer cannot spin it safely.

Ub.what_it_means: The load has gone off balance in the tub and the washer will not spin it at speed, because an unbalanced drum at spin speed can damage the machine.
Ub.why_it_happens: Usually one heavy item on its own — a towel, a bath mat, a single pair of jeans — or a load that has twisted into a rope on one side of the drum.
Ub.what_to_try: Open the door, redistribute the load by hand and restart the spin. Adding a couple of similar-weight items often settles it; washing one heavy item alone rarely spins well.
Ub.when_to_call: If it trips on every load including well-balanced ones, the suspension or the sensor reading the drum may need looking at.

UE.what_it_means: The same unbalanced-load condition as Ub, shown as UE on some Samsung models.
UE.why_it_happens: A single heavy item, or a load that has bunched to one side of the drum.
UE.what_to_try: Redistribute the load by hand and restart the spin.
UE.when_to_call: If balanced loads also trip it, the drum suspension is worth checking.

codes.meaning: Water is not draining at the rate it should, or is not draining at all.

SE.what_it_means: Water is not leaving the machine at the rate the cycle expects, or is not leaving at all. Shown as 5E, SE, 5C or nd depending on the panel.
SE.why_it_happens: The debris filter at the bottom front catches coins, hair grips and lint and eventually packs solid. A kinked drain hose or a standpipe that cannot take the flow does the same thing from further down the line.
SE.what_to_try: Open the small flap at the bottom front, drain the residual water into a tray and clean the filter. Then check the drain hose behind the machine for kinks and that it is not pushed too far into the standpipe.
SE.when_to_call: If the filter is clean and the hose run is clear, the drain pump itself needs testing.

5C.what_it_means: The same not-draining fault as 5E and SE, shown as 5C on some Samsung panels.
5C.why_it_happens: A packed debris filter at the bottom front, a kinked drain hose, or a standpipe that cannot take the flow.
5C.what_to_try: Clean the filter behind the flap at the bottom front, draining the residual water into a tray first, then check the hose run behind the machine.
5C.when_to_call: If the filter is clean and the hose is clear, the drain pump needs testing.

codes.meaning: The door is not being detected as closed and locked, so the cycle will not run.

dC.what_it_means: The washer cannot confirm the door is shut and locked, so it will not start or will stop mid-cycle.
dC.why_it_happens: Most often laundry caught in the door seal stopping it closing flush, or a door that has been slammed rather than pushed shut.
dC.what_to_try: Open the door fully, clear anything caught around the seal, and close it firmly without forcing it. Check the latch and the strike plate for anything obstructing them.
dC.when_to_call: If nothing is obstructing it and the lock still will not engage, the door lock assembly is the usual cause.

codes.meaning: An over-sudsing condition has been detected and the machine is pausing to let the foam clear.

SUd.what_it_means: The washer has detected far more foam than the drum is designed to handle, and is pausing to clear it before continuing.
SUd.why_it_happens: Usually too much detergent, or a standard detergent used in a high-efficiency machine, which foams several times more than an HE formula.
SUd.what_to_try: Let the machine run its own suds-clearing routine rather than cutting the cycle short. Next load, reduce the dose and check the detergent is HE-rated if your machine needs one.
SUd.when_to_call: If it appears with a correct HE dose, something may be holding water in the drum and it is worth having checked.

codes.meaning: There is too much water in the washer, which normally means the inlet valve is passing water when it should be shut.

OE.what_it_means: There is more water in the tub than there should be, so the washer has stopped filling and is trying to pump out.
OE.why_it_happens: Normally the inlet valve passing water when it has been told to close, rather than anything to do with the load or detergent.
OE.what_to_try: Turn the supply taps off at the wall so no more water can arrive. There is no owner-side fix for a valve that will not shut.
OE.when_to_call: Promptly — a valve stuck open is a flood risk as well as an error code.

0E.what_it_means: The same overfill condition as OE, shown with a zero on some panels.
0E.why_it_happens: An inlet valve letting water through when it should be closed.
0E.what_to_try: Shut the taps at the wall to stop the fill. Nothing else here is an owner check.
0E.when_to_call: Promptly, for the same reason as OE.

codes.meaning: The AddWash door is not registering as closed and latched.

ddC.what_it_means: The AddWash door — the small hatch in the main door — is not registering as closed and latched.
ddC.why_it_happens: It is easy to push shut without seating the catch, and a trapped sock or glove will stop it closing flush.
ddC.what_to_try: Open the AddWash door fully, clear anything caught in it, and press it closed until the catch engages.
ddC.when_to_call: If it is properly shut and still reads open, the hatch switch needs checking.

codes.meaning: Moisture has been detected somewhere inside the machine that it should not be, which is a leak rather than a setting.
A fault in the heater circuit, so the machine cannot bring the water up to temperature.

HE.what_it_means: A fault in the heater circuit, so the machine cannot bring the wash water up to the temperature the cycle asked for.
HE.why_it_happens: A component failure rather than anything that builds up, so it usually appears without warning.
HE.what_to_try: Nothing here is an owner check — the heater and its circuit are inside the machine.
HE.when_to_call: When you see it. Cold-water cycles may still run, but the machine is not doing what the programme selected.

codes.meaning: A motor fault — the drive is not behaving as the control expects.
The temperature sensor is reporting a reading outside the range the cycle allows.
A button on the control panel is reading as stuck or continuously pressed.
The detergent drawer has not been pushed fully closed.
Not a fault — Child Lock is active, so the panel is ignoring input until it is released.
An irregularity in the electrical supply reaching the machine has interrupted the cycle.
